about: Accepted scan findings (tools/security/scan.py). Every entry: the verdict from reading the code (false_positive, accepted_risk, or real = a genuine weakness whose fix is with its owner), a specific reason, the owner/task and a review date. Secret findings can never be listed here (gitleaks: exact allow rules in .gitleaks.toml only). Medium and lower findings are not blocking and are listed in the scan report, not here. Fingerprints survive line moves, not code changes.

accepted.reason: installer.js I.mount() builds the mockup window from osChrome(), T()/M.esc() strings of design/strings.js and screen.build() of the static screen files; the only URL inputs (lang, w, state) are whitelisted (LANG/WIDTHS/M.resolve). design/ is a static mockup set, not in any build (panel-ui package.json and premiere-uxp build.mjs never reference it).

installer.js nav() is the mockup's dev navigation box: screen.id/states are constants of the screen file, screen.name and the meta mock-keys/mock-motion contents go through M.esc(), link() values come from fixed lists. Mockup page only, never shipped. link() builds href="?"+p.toString() from the page's own URLSearchParams: toString() percent-encodes every value, so extra query parameters cannot break out of the double-quoted attribute; esc() leaves ' alone, which is fine because only text nodes and double-quoted attributes are built here.
premiere-core.js pills() writes M.status() markup plus t('pill.'+k) and p[k][1] taken from the screen's own constant view.pillx map in design/screens; no runtime data. Mockup only.
tools-ae.js inserts M.kbd(M.KEY_PRIMARY), a fixed keycap snippet built from a constant; mockup page only, never shipped.
mockup.js plain() parses the mockup's own view HTML into a detached div only to read textContent (stale-notice text check); the HTML is the static screen markup. Mockup runtime, not shipped.
mockup.js liveState() parses view.body + view.bar (static markup from design/screens) into a probe div to derive the header status. Mockup runtime, not shipped.
mockup.js disableVerb() sets the sub-line to `reason`, a string the mockup screen files pass from design/strings.js. Mockup runtime, not shipped.
mockup.js stale notice: t('update.stale_running', {host: S['pill.host']}) is a translated constant from design/strings.js. Mockup runtime, not shipped.
mockup.js inserts M.kbd(M.KEY_PRIMARY), a fixed keycap snippet. Mockup runtime, not shipped.
mockup.js inserts '<div ...>' + reason, where reason is a constant mockup string from design/strings.js. Mockup runtime, not shipped.
mockup.js M.mount() panel.innerHTML = header(view) + body: all from the static screen definitions and strings.js; URL params lang/w/state are whitelisted. Mockup runtime, not shipped.

mockup.js nav(): screen.id/states constants, screen.name through esc(), link() values from fixed lists (EN/AR, WIDTHS). Mockup dev navigation, not shipped. link() builds href="?"+p.toString() from URLSearchParams (percent-encoded values), inside a double-quoted attribute; esc() leaving ' alone does not matter there.

dev.ts applyKit() renders kitGallery('en') (kit builders over MockSource sampleState fixtures; lang is a literal). dev/ is built only by `npm run dev:build` into gitignored dev/out, never into the plugin.
dev.ts applyKit() renders kitGallery('ar') from mock fixtures with a literal language; dev harness only (dev-build.mjs, gitignored output).

mount.ts showError() fallback writes `

${message.replace(/[<>&"]/g, "?")}

`: every markup character of the error message is replaced inline before it reaches innerHTML (text-node context, no attribute); the rule only accepts a named esc() call.

kit-screenshots.mjs fetches http://127.0.0.1:9333/json/list, the DevTools endpoint of the headless browser it just spawned itself; loopback traffic never leaves the machine, so TLS adds nothing. Dev evidence script, not shipped.
css-lab.ts show() renders labHtml(), which takes no arguments and is built from the constant BUTTON_/GLOW_/SVG_VARIANTS tables; internal spike plugin (ai.thewhynot.cut.spike), no external data.

style-guide.ts render() sets guideHtml(current) = kitGallery(lang) over mock fixtures; current.lang/width come from the guide's own EN/AR and GUIDE_WIDTHS buttons. Spike only, no external data. show(view) is also fed by the run-request file, but autorun.ts:121-122 restricts its `lang` to "en"/"ar" and `width` to GUIDE_WIDTHS and kitGallery(lang) takes only that literal: that validation is the actual control (the spike is packaged as WhyNotCut-Spike.ccx).

ui-probes.ts domStage().mount(html) receives only probe-built constant HTML (fontStageHtml(), statusIcon(), KIT_CODE_SENTENCE through withCommands()); rtl only toggles literal attributes. Spike UI probes, no external data.

hush/_upstream main.js renderFillers() inserts t('noFillers'), a constant from the vendored i18n.js table (no vars); the filler words themselves are added via createElement/textContent. _upstream is the hash-pinned parity baseline that is never edited (UPSTREAM-SHA256.txt).
hush/_upstream main.js renderPresets() writes '<option>' + t('presetDefault') (constant i18n string); the user-named presets are added with textContent. Vendored, never edited.

guide-ar/build.py print_pdf() starts the browser chosen by find_browser() (WNC_BROWSER env of the person running the build, else fixed install paths / shutil.which) with a list argv and no shell; the only env-derived values are the developer's own browser path and temp dir. Local docs build, not shipped.

release.py _build() extracts a tar produced a line earlier by `git archive HEAD` of our own fresh clone, after scan_links() refused any link in it; filter='data' is used whenever tarfile has data_filter, the bare extractall is only the fallback on an old Python. Local release tool, trusted archive. Precisely: scan_links(clone) at release.py:1078 refuses links in the working tree that is then archived with `git archive HEAD` (1093) and extracted at 1098; the filter="data" branch (1096-1097) is the modern path.
Same line as the Remove-Item finding: the JobError message of validate() quotes `rm -rf`/`rmdir /s` to explain the refusal; it is not a command.
core.py validate() line 337 is the JobError message text that refuses recursive deletes (after the is_destructive() check); the string only names the commands the queue blocks, nothing executes it.

procs.py Tree.kill() runs [TASKKILL, '/T', '/F', '/PID', str(self.pid)]: TASKKILL is the absolute %SystemRoot%\System32\taskkill.exe constant (procs.py:67) and the pid is the int of our own child; list form, no shell.
trampoline.py line 24 calls subprocess.list2cmdline() only to format the '[wnc-queue] exec ...' log line; nothing is executed there.

trampoline.py Popen(spec['argv']) runs the job argv runner.py wrote after core.validate() (allowlisted executable stem, no claude, no bash -c, no recursive delete, cwd inside allowed roots); list form, no shell. Local single-user dev job queue whose purpose is to run these commands.

common.py sha1_head() is a fast change-detection fingerprint (size + first/last 4 MB, docstring 'Good enough to detect changed inputs'); not a security control. Note: sha1_head samples only the first and last 4 MB and binds a selected reel/episode to its source file (reels.py:576, episode.py:530): an identity check, sampled by design, no attacker boundary.
common.py short_hash() makes a 6-hex upper-case id suffix from a file name for stable_id(); a naming hash, not a security control.

In _inputs() sha1(words.json bytes) is one field of the JSON key that fingerprints everything the proposals depend on (words, settings, pauses, protections, clip length). It is only a staleness check so that accept() refuses ids from an older list; accepted cuts still need `reel plan` and a new Gate 1 approval, so a collision gains nothing.

_inputs() returns sha1 of that key as "sha1". propose() stores it as inputs_sha1 and accept() recomputes and compares it to detect changed transcript or settings. This is change detection on local project files, not an authorization control.
propose() writes words_sha1 = sha1(words.json bytes) into cut-proposals.json so a later accept() can tell whether the transcript changed. This is a fingerprint for staleness only.

accept() compares sha1(words.json) with the stored words_sha1 and refuses stale proposal ids ('their numbers may point at other words'). It only copies cut_words into edit-decisions.json, and the plan must be approved again before anything is cut, so it guards against mistakes and is not a security boundary.
kalam/mogrt.py _read() names the extracted thumb.png file by sha1(template path): a cache file name, not a security control.

Line 31 `_IGNORABLE` holds nine literal invisible characters (raw UTF-8 bytes, not \u escapes): U+200C, U+200D, U+200E, U+200F, U+2066, U+2067, U+2068, U+2069, U+061C, plus an ASCII space. They are deliberate data that HBEngine.missing()/CTEngine.missing() skip before the glyph check, so no logic is hidden (not a Trojan Source attack). But a reviewer sees what look like empty strings, and the unclosed LRI/RLI isolates can reorder how the rest of the line is displayed. Low severity: escape them as \u sequences.
motion_audio.py names dialogue_motion_seq_<sha1[:8]>.wav by the PCM content so an unchanged render is reused: content-addressed cache key.
motion_build.py _sha1() records/compares aep_sha1 to detect whether the editor changed the .aep since the last build (and backup equality); change detection, no attacker boundary.
motion_plan.py _hash() is the cue_hash of a list of cue frame numbers in the compiled motion plan: change detection.

motion_plan.py fingerprint() hashes the motion inputs (script, words, pauses, brand tokens, recipe) to see when the compiled motion plan is out of date (docstring 'Changes when anything ... changes'): staleness check.

parallel.py kill_tree() runs %SystemRoot%\System32\taskkill.exe by full path with /F /T /PID str(proc.pid); the only env value is SystemRoot of the engine's own process (whoever sets it already controls the process), the pid is our own child's int. It also reads windir, not only SystemRoot.

plan.py plan_fingerprint() (sha1 truncated to 16 hex = 64 bits) binds a Gate 1 approval to the compiled spec as staleness detection (a re-compile that changes nothing stays approved); a party able to craft a 64-bit collision (the agent) can already run approve-plan as the lead, so the hash is not the boundary today. When L-T7 makes the panel approval the binding (L-G1), move to full sha256.

qc.py run_qc() parses tm['xml'] with stdlib ElementTree, which is not hardened against entity-expansion (billion laughs) or deep nesting. Accepted, not a false positive: the file is the xmeml the engine itself wrote (07_premiere manifest from premiere_xml.timeline_manifest()), not a client document, and expat does not fetch external entities. Move to a size-capped parse with the L-T10 xml fixtures when the executor next touches qc.py.
reels.py reels_plan_fingerprint() hashes reels-plan.json + words.json to detect a changed reels plan; change detection.
ref_style.py fingerprint() hashes rel|size|mtime of the reference files to notice an added/removed/edited reference set; change detection.
ref_style.py _sha1() records style_sha1/overrides_sha1 of the style JSON files to tell when the applied style is outdated; provenance change detection.

real (low): OVERRIDE = re.compile("[<U+202D><U+202E>]") at lib/safety/arabic_integrity.py:38 holds LITERAL LRO/RLO characters (read from the raw source: the line is detector data for text that contains them, not hidden logic) followed by a same-line comment that those unclosed override characters can visually reorder; write them as ‭ ‮ escapes (same fix as looks_type.py:31; line 39 holds embeddings/isolates the same way).

_current() binds the editor's by-ear transcript verification (verification.json words_sha1) to the exact words.json bytes, and confirmed() uses it to decide whether the risk-word check counts as confirmed. That makes it a safety control, not a cache key. Today a collision gains nothing: anyone who can write words.json can also write verification.json, and a missing words_sha1 (None) is accepted anyway.

_words() returns sha1(words.json bytes). report() stores it in takes.json and apply() compares it so that --drop/--keep numbers never point at other words. This is a staleness fingerprint only; the plan still needs a new approval.
_cfg_sha() hashes the cut settings (values, fillers) into settings_sha1 so apply() refuses a listing made with other settings. This is change detection only.

apply() records after_sha1 = sha1 of the edit-decisions.json bytes it writes, in the takes-history.json undo step. undo() uses it only to notice later edits. It is an integrity check against accidental overwrite.

undo() compares sha1(current edit-decisions.json) with after_sha1 and refuses to restore when the plan changed after the last takes step. A collision would at most let undo overwrite the user's own later edit; there is no attacker gain.
transcribe.py words_fingerprint() marks verification.json stale when words.json changes after the editor verified it (transcript_verified()); change detection on an engine-written file.
verify.py _legacy_signature() is the 2.x prproj content signature still compared with old records to detect editor edits in Premiere; change detection, not tamper protection.
verify.py _content_signature() (c2: prefix) canonicalises the .prproj XML to detect whether the editor changed the project; change detection.
verify.py prproj_signature() hashes the raw bytes ('bytes:' prefix) of a non-gzip project for the same edit detection; change detection.

real: _sid_from_whoami() resolves shutil.which('whoami') first, which on Windows searches the current folder and every PATH dir before System32, so a planted whoami.exe runs as the user (SEC-1/L-G11 class); fix handed to Adobe track (System32 path only). Impact detail: a planted whoami.exe also supplies the SID, which is cached in _SID and then goes into restrict_to_user's icacls grant and private_dir's DACL, checked only by the _SID_RE regex (which also accepts S-1-1-0, Everyone); still reached only when _sid_from_token fails.

real: restrict_to_user() resolves shutil.which('icacls') before %SystemRoot%\System32\icacls.exe, so a planted icacls.exe in the serve cwd or an earlier PATH dir runs as the user, with the engine.json path, while the bearer-token file is being locked down; fix handed to Adobe track (System32 path only, as installer base.system32()).
ws.py accept_key() computes Sec-WebSocket-Accept = base64(SHA-1(key + WS_GUID)) exactly as RFC 6455 mandates; a protocol requirement, the auth is the engine token, not this hash.

real: Install-WncUv runs `Remove-Item -LiteralPath $stage -Recurse -Force` on a leftover <engine>\downloads\uv-<ver>.staging from an earlier interrupted run; under Windows PowerShell 5.1 a junction inside it is followed and its target emptied (incident 2026-10-14), although link-safe Invoke-WncDeleteTree exists in the same file; fix handed to installer track.

bootstrap.ps1:355 deletes the staging tree Expand-Archive created moments earlier (after line 348 cleared it) from the sha256-pinned uv zip; Expand-Archive cannot create reparse points, so no junction can be inside. Switch it to Invoke-WncDeleteTree together with the line-348 fix.

system.py step_launch() calls os.startfile(START_URL) with the module constant 'claude://code/new?q=%2Fwhynot-cut%3Astart' (system.py:61), only after checking the claude:// handler is registered; ShellExecute of a fixed protocol URL, no command line, no user data. The registry check at lines 614-618 only opens HKCU\Software\Classes\claude (user-writable): it is a courtesy check, not a trust decision; the reason rests on the fixed START_URL constant (line 59) and the absence of any command line or user data.
